page.layout: One page of text in verse with italic mottoes and headings; a manuscript Greek annotation in the lower margin left; a bracket beside lines; a handwritten Greek note at the foot (not printed, so not transcribed). Running head at top; page number 120 at top left.

main_text.p: Viuida tum coelo surgent suspiria: tumque Quaesitum tangent feruida vota polum.

head.i: Non medicus, sed morbus causa mali. Peccatum malorum causa.

main_text.p: Vis ferri flammaeque secat quod putria membra, Non medicus, verum morbus id acer agit.
Vastatas urbes ferro quod cernis & igne, Peccatum causa est, culpa nec vlla Dei.
Evolat, aduerso mutatus frigore, feruor, Fornacis clausae sint nisi saepe fores.
Sic mens, quae laxo nimium blaterauerit ore, Diffluit, & constat vix bene firma sibi.

head.i: Coniunctis luminibus tueri. Mens vaga verum non cernit.

main_text.p: Non potes oculo bene cernere, si vaga currant Lumina, nec fixo stent requieta loco.
Sic vaga mens mundi curā distracta fugacis, Non vlla verum cernere parte potest.

head.i: Tristitiam terrenam caelestis gaudiy spes absorbet.

main_text.p: Parua lacus magni fundum scintilla subintrans, Articulo minimo temporis obruitur.
Tristitiae molem terrenae gaudia caeli Absorbent nullo deperitura die.

head.i: Aqua iactu lapidis turbida. Mens duris verbis turbata.

main_text.p: Si lapis in vitream coniectus decidit vndam, Turbatur motae splendor amoenus aquae.

page.notes: Printed text is partly damaged and faded at the right and left edges; some letters are uncertain. A handwritten Greek annotation at the foot and manuscript marks are not transcribed. The bracket at left marks the Tristitia emblem. The catchword "In pa-" is treated as a foot line.
